[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance provides step-by-step instructions for authoring Claude Code Commands — the reusable workflow triggers that invoke Skills and orchestrate multi-step operations. Commands are the Claude Code-specific implementation of the Workflow construct category in the unified taxonomy ([ADR-TEC-020](../../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md)). This guidance implements [STD-TEC-AI-004](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-004-workflow-authoring.md) for the Claude Code platform and covers naming conventions, step structure, intent routing, parameter handling, and the relationship between Commands and Skills.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Consistency** — All Commands follow the same structural pattern, making them discoverable and predictable
- **Reusability** — Well-authored Commands compose cleanly with Skills and can be invoked across projects
- **Onboarding speed** — New team members discover available workflows through the standardized Command catalog
- **Cross-vendor mapping** — Commands authored to this guidance map cleanly to GitHub Copilot Prompts (see [GUID-TECH-IMPL-007](./GUID-TECH-IMPL-007-github-copilot-prompt-authoring-guidance.md))

- **Secondary**: Platform engineers maintaining the shared `.claude/commands/` catalog

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Without authoring guidance, teams create Commands with inconsistent naming, unclear step ordering, and ambiguous Skill routing — resulting in Commands that fail silently or produce unexpected behavior.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

A Claude Code Command is a Markdown file placed in `.claude/commands/` that provides multi-step instructions the agent follows when a user invokes the Command by name (e.g., `/pr-appr-review`, `/eap-appr-pr`, `/eap-convert`). Commands differ from Skills in that:

| Construct | Purpose | Invocation | Persistence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | Domain expertise and behavioral constraints | Loaded automatically by context | Persistent across session |
| **Command** | Workflow trigger with sequential steps | Explicitly invoked by user (`/<name>`) | Single execution |
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#taxonomy-relationship]

### Taxonomy Relationship

Per [ADR-TEC-020](../../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md), Commands map to the **Workflow** category — they are defined, reusable multi-step operational patterns that coordinate Skills and Tools toward a repeatable outcome.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#command-file-structure]

### Command File Structure

Every Command MUST be a single Markdown file with the following structure:

```markdown
<Intent statement — one sentence describing what this command accomplishes>

1. <Step 1 — imperative action>
2. <Step 2 — imperative action>
3. <Step 3 — imperative action>
...

<Optional closing instruction — what to report when done>
```

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#command-namespace-slug]

#### Command Namespace Slug

The `eap-` prefix is the **command namespace slug** for repositories derived from [EAP Bootstrap](https://github.com/mygainwell/eap-bootstrap). It identifies the template lineage and prevents naming collisions when multiple repos are open in the same AI coding assistant session.

**Ref-architecture-unique exception**: Commands authored uniquely for `eap-ref-architecture` itself — not synced from or shared with a bootstrap template — MAY omit the slug entirely, using unprefixed `<noun>[-<verb>].md` (e.g., `adr.md`, `pattern.md`, `standard.md`, `tech-eval.md`, `activity-brief.md`). There is no template-lineage collision risk for these Commands because they never exist outside this repository. New bootstrap-derived or bootstrap-synced Commands MUST still use the slug.

Each template defines its own slug derived from the repository naming convention for that project type:

| Project Type | Repository Naming Convention | Template | Slug | Example Commands |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EAP Bootstrap** | `eap-bootstrap` | [eap-bootstrap](https://github.com/mygainwell/eap-bootstrap) | `eap-` | `eap-lint.md`, `eap-appr-pr.md` |
| **Product Monolithic** | `{product-line-abr}-{product-abr}` | [ets-bootstrap](https://github.com/mygainwell/ets-bootstrap) | `{product-line-abr}-{product-abr}-` | `pfe-pg-lint.md`, `pfe-ps-appr-pr.md` |
| **Product Modular** | `{product-line-abr}-{product-abr}-{module-abr}` | [ets-bootstrap](https://github.com/mygainwell/ets-bootstrap) | `{product-line-abr}-{product-abr}-{module-abr}-` | `mms-cms-cef-lint.md` |
| **Account (State)** | `{account}-{state-abr}-{product or module-abr}` | [ets-bootstrap](https://github.com/mygainwell/ets-bootstrap) | `{account}-{state-abr}-{product-abr}-` | `act-ca-edw-lint.md` |

All examples in this document use the `eap-` prefix. Substitute your project's own slug when applying this convention.

#### File and Invocation Conventions

| Rule | Convention | Example |

| File name | `<slug>[<phase>-]<noun>[-<verb>].md` | `eap-branch.md`, `eap-appr-pr.md`, `pr-appr-resolve.md` |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#phase-abbreviations]

#### Phase Abbreviations

| Phase | Abbreviation | SDD Phase |
|---|---|---|
| Discover | `disc` | Pre-specification — capability survey, RE, requirements derivation. **Note:** `disc` is a documented Variation in PTN-TEC-AI-005, not one of the six formal SDD pipeline stages. It represents pre-specification work that precedes Specification. |
| Specify | `spec` | Specification — BDD authoring |
| Gate | `gate` | Completeness Gate — quality audit |
| Decompose | `decom` | Decomposition — design, scaffold, IaC |
| Approve | `appr` | Human Approval — PR, review, merge, dispatch |
| Govern | `gov` | Governance — enterprise ADRs, patterns, standards (ref-arch only) |
| *(omitted)* | | Cross-cutting and DevOps/utility commands — no phase prefix |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#naming-decision-tree]

### Naming Decision Tree

```
Is the Command SDD pipeline-specific?
├── Yes →
│   Use slug + phase prefix + noun[-verb]: <slug><phase>-<noun>[-<verb>].md
│   (e.g., eap-appr-pr.md, pr-appr-resolve.md)
└── No →
    Use slug + noun[-verb] (no phase): <slug><noun>[-<verb>].md
    (e.g., eap-branch.md, eap-doc-status.md)

Does it accept arguments?
├── Yes → Document expected arguments in the intent statement
└── No → Omit $ARGUMENTS references

Verb guidance: omit when noun alone is unambiguous (<slug>lint, <slug>push);
use noun-verb when the artifact has a lifecycle (<slug>spec-fr-create vs <slug>spec-fr-modify).
```
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#step-authoring-rules]

### Step Authoring Rules

1. **Start with context gathering** — Read relevant files before taking action.
2. **Use imperative verbs** — "Create", "Read", "Verify", "Run", "Update" (not "You should" or "Consider").
3. **Be explicit about file paths** — Use relative paths from repository root.
4. **Include conditional logic** — Use "If [condition], then [action]" for branches.
5. **End with a completion signal** — Tell the agent what to report or verify when done.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#intent-routing]

### Intent Routing

When a Command invokes Skills, it MUST route to them explicitly:

```markdown
Determine the appropriate skill based on the file type:
- If the file is a standard → Read `.claude/skills/architect/SKILL.md`
- If the file is an EA artifact → Read `.claude/skills/ea-reviewer/SKILL.md`
- If the file is documentation → Read `.claude/skills/documenter/SKILL.md`
```
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#command-invocation-boundary]

### Command Invocation Boundary

Commands MAY reference other Commands via slash-form invocation (e.g., "`/pr-appr-review`") per [STD-TEC-AI-004](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-004-workflow-authoring.md) MR-9. When doing so, Commands MUST NOT create invocation cycles (Command A → Command B → Command A), and MUST document cross-Command references in their intent statement.

For each step in a Command, prefer the composition mechanism that best matches the work:

- **Route to a Skill** — for AI-reasoning-dependent steps: `Read .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (see Intent Routing above and [PTN-TEC-AI-004](../../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-004-skill-composition-and-orchestration-pattern.md))
- **Shell/Task target** — for deterministic sequential operations (lint, push, version): run `task <target>` directly; no LLM involvement needed
- **Cross-Command reference (slash-form)** — for reusing a governed Command as a step: reference it by slash-name and document the dependency; referential integrity (the target Command must exist) and acyclicity are mandatory per MR-9
- **Claude Code Workflow** — for multi-agent orchestration requiring isolated per-agent context

**Single-dispatch routing exception:** A Command that performs AI-reasoned content analysis and routes to one Skill based on the result is acceptable conditional composition per PTN-TEC-AI-004 Mode 2. The Command must document this with a "Pattern note" in its intent statement (e.g., "Routes to `/modeler` or `/presenter` based on content analysis — single-dispatch router").
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#parameter-handling]

### Parameter Handling

Commands that accept arguments use the `$ARGUMENTS` variable:

```markdown
Convert the document specified in $ARGUMENTS to the target format.

1. Determine the source file extension from $ARGUMENTS
2. Select the appropriate converter based on extension:
   - `.md` → md2pdf or md2docx
   - `.docx` → docx2md
   - `.pptx` → pptx2md or pptx2pdf
3. Run the converter from the repository root
4. Report the output file location
```

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#decision-tree-when-to-create-a-command]

### Decision Tree: When to Create a Command

```
Is it a one-liner operation (read a file, run a command, search code)?
├── Yes → Use a Tool directly — no Command needed
└── No →
    Is it a named, repeatable workflow (create PR, write specs, check architecture)?
    ├── Yes → Create a Command in .claude/commands/
    └── No →
        Does it require a specific expertise role (design, review, document, evaluate)?
        ├── Yes → Use a Skill (/architect, /ea-reviewer, /documenter…)
        └── No →
            Does it touch an external system (ADO story, GitHub issue, PR link)?
            ├── Yes → Use an MCP Server tool (mcp__ado__*, mcp__github__*)
            └── No →
                Is it large-scale, parallel, or needs adversarial verification?
                ├── Yes → Use a Workflow (orchestrates multiple Skills/Commands)
                └── No →
                    Do you want to review the plan before anything is executed?
                    ├── Yes → Use Plan Mode (/plan)
                    └── No → Ask Copilot directly — no construct needed
```
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#supplemental-heuristics]

#### Supplemental Heuristics

| Signal | Recommended Construct |
|--------|----------------------|
| One-time question or explanation | Ask directly — no construct needed |
| One-liner operation (read a file, run a command) | Use a Tool directly — no construct needed |
| Recurring task with defined steps | Command |
| Role-specific expertise or conventions | Skill |
| Spans requirements → design → code → test → docs | Workflow (Command that orchestrates multiple Skills) |
| Multiple agents need to edit files in parallel without conflicts | Worktrees (`isolation: "worktree"`) |
| Recurring or time-based execution | Cron / Wakeup |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#command-quality-checklist]

### Command Quality Checklist

- [ ] File is in `.claude/commands/` named per the Naming Conventions above (`<slug>[<phase>-]<noun>[-<verb>].md`, or unprefixed `<noun>[-<verb>].md` under the documented ref-architecture-unique exception)
- [ ] First line is a clear intent statement (one sentence)
- [ ] Steps are numbered and use imperative verbs
- [ ] File paths are relative to repository root
- [ ] Conditional branches use "If/then" structure
- [ ] Skill references use explicit paths (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`)
- [ ] Steps invoke Skills (by reading `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) for AI-reasoning steps; cross-Command references use slash-form per STD-TEC-AI-004 MR-9 (referential integrity and acyclicity required)
- [ ] `$ARGUMENTS` is documented if the command accepts parameters
- [ ] Command ends with a completion/reporting instruction
- [ ] No secrets or environment-specific values embedded
- [ ] A corresponding GitHub Copilot Prompt exists or is planned (see [PTN-TEC-AI-003](../../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md))
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#minimum-viable-command]

### Minimum Viable Command

```markdown
Run the project linters and report results.

1. Activate the Python virtual environment at `.utils/.venv/`
2. Run `black --check` on all Python files in `.utils/`
3. Run `ruff check` on all Python files in `.utils/`
4. Report pass/fail status for each linter
```
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#command-with-skill-routing]

### Command with Skill Routing

```markdown
Create a new architectural pattern in the appropriate domain.

1. Determine the domain: Application, Business, Governance, Information, Infrastructure, ITSM-Operations, Security, or Technology
2. Determine the pattern type (e.g., api, integration, event-driven, deployment)
3. Derive a kebab-case title slug from $ARGUMENTS (lowercase; spaces and punctuation converted to hyphens; any IDs or flags stripped)
4. Find the next available pattern number in `patterns/<domain>/<type>/`
5. Copy the template from `resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/pattern.md`
6. Create `patterns/<domain>/<type>/PTN-<DOMAIN>-<TYPE>-<NNN>-<title-slug>-pattern.md`
7. Fill in: problem, solution, context, consequences, implementation guidance
8. Review against `patterns/pattern-quality-checklist.md`
9. Update `patterns/<domain>/README.md` to include the new pattern
10. Set status to "Proposed" until reviewed

Patterns should be technology-agnostic solutions to recurring problems.
```
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md#command-with-parameters]

### Command with Parameters

```markdown
Convert the file specified in $ARGUMENTS to the requested format.

1. Parse $ARGUMENTS to identify the source file path and target format
2. Verify the source file exists
3. Select the converter based on file extension mapping
4. Run the conversion tool from the repository root: `python .utils/formatters/<tool>/<script>.py <file>`
5. Report the output file path and any conversion warnings
```
